[![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/lukmanovr/dkr/blob/main/homeworks/hw01_foundations.ipynb)

**≈ 5–10 hours · individual work · 10% of the course grade**

One notebook, three parts, covering representations, classical graph ML, shallow
embeddings, and KG embedding theory:

- **Part A · Derivations (30 pts).** Four proofs, answered in markdown cells:
  relabeling and spectral invariance (plus finding where the invariant *fails*);
  why PageRank needs its teleport, on the smallest graph that breaks it; the SGNS
  fixed point, derived; and the complete DistMult column of the Week 4 cheat sheet.
- **Part B · Implementation (60 pts, autograded).** Three exercises whose asserts you
  can read: spectral fingerprints that catch A1's cospectral pair; an empirical
  verification that SGNS converges to the shifted PMI (theory, then `corr > 0.9` in
  code); and DistMult trained for 1,500 steps that *provably* cannot learn direction
  — your proof from A4, caught on camera.
- **Part C · Investigation (10 pts).** One hyperparameter from Labs 2–4, one
  mechanistic hypothesis, at most three runs, ten honest lines. Null results welcome;
  cherry-picking is not.

## Rubric

| Part | Points | Graded by |
|---|---|---|
| A1 spectra · A2 PageRank · A3 SGNS · A4 DistMult | 10 + 8 + 6 + 6 | TA, per proof step |
| B1 · B2 · B3 | 20 + 20 + 20 | autograder (visible + hidden variants) |
| C hypothesis · experiment · conclusion | 2 + 4 + 4 | TA |

Late policy: −10% per day, up to 3 days; nothing accepted after solutions are
released. Regrade window: one week after grades post.

## FAQ

**Can I hand-write Part A?** Yes — paste a *legible* photo into the markdown cell.
Illegible scans are graded as blank.

**The visible asserts pass — am I guaranteed the B points?** Almost: hidden variants
run the same checks with different graphs and toy vectors. If your code is honest
(no hard-coded answers), visible-pass ≈ hidden-pass.

**May I use an AI assistant?** Yes, with disclosure in the final cell (tool + what
for), per the [honor code]. You must be able to explain any line and any proof step
in person; inability to explain is treated as undeclared use.

**Part C says "at most three configurations" — can I run ten?** You can *run*
anything; you must *report* a focused comparison. The point is a defensible
conclusion, not a sweep.

**Something is broken / ambiguous.** Post in the course forum thread for HW1 —
clarifications get pinned there, and everyone sees the same answers.
